name: crypto-ed25519-verify
algorithm: std Ed25519 (RFC 8032) Verify, n times over 256 signed 64-byte messages under one key, the last signature corrupted (mk/crypto-ed25519-verify.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard Ed25519
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no Ed25519; no crate stands in

notes: Work per step: one verification of one 64-byte message: S checked canonical, A decoded, SHA-512 of R, A and message, the double multiplication [S]B - [k]A. Mk crypto.Ed25519.Verify and Go ed25519.Verify then encode the result and compare it with R bytewise (cofactorless). Zig Signature.verifyStrict is cofactorless too (CRY-3; Signature.verify, cofactored, would multiply S, A and R by 8 and accept more), but it also decodes R (one square root, about one field exponentiation), rejects an identity A, an identity R and a non-canonical R, and compares points: more work than Mk and Go, labelled here. Verifications per second = n / median.

Checksums: every column printed the same value at the quick and the publish args in `go run ./tools/bench verify` and `verify -publish-size` (mk built from the tree, Zig 0.17.0, Go 1.27.3) on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07 (std-crypto session 1, with the public half as a third argument; session 2, after D-319, with the key from Ed25519.FromSeed: the same checksums; session 3, with Zig's verifyStrict: the same checksums). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
